analysis_steps.goal: Fit Keplerian orbit geometry to T1 ring

method.value: Least-squares fitting of orbital elements to loci of the ring

evidence.quote: By least-square fitting to the loci, we determined the orbital parameters: the semimajor axis ($a$), eccentricity ($e$), longitude of ascending node ($\Omega$), argument of pericenter ($\omega$), and inclination angle ($i$).
We placed the dynamical center at $(l,\ b)=(-0\ensuremath{^\circ}.0841,\ -0\ensuremath{^\circ}.0957)$
we performed orbital fitting to the T1 ring assuming a Keplerian motion.

By least-square fitting to the loci, we determined the orbital parameters: the semimajor axis ($a$), eccentricity ($e$), longitude of ascending node ($\Omega$), argument of pericenter ($\omega$), and inclination angle ($i$).
The best-fit orbit is projected in Figures 3(a) and (b).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit dynamical mass and systemic velocity

method.value: Chi-square minimization of observed moment-1 velocities along the ring

evidence.quote: we estimated the mass ($M_{\rm dyn}$) and line-of-sight velocity ($V_{\rm sys}$) of the dynamical center by fitting the observed velocities on the T1 ring with a chi-square ($\chi^2$) minimization approach.
we used the moment-1 values of the CS image smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of $1.5\ensuremath{''}$ FWHM
The distance to the Galactic center is assumed to be $D=8$ kpc.

findings_qualitative.value: HCN–0.085–0.094 resolves into three clumps T1–T3 with broad velocity widths; T1 has a ring with steep velocity gradient

evidence.quote: HCN–0.085–0.094 is resolved into three major clumps (labeled as T1, T2, and T3), which are clearly traced in all the three lines.

claims.hypothesis: T1 orbits an invisible massive object
claims.experiment: Keplerian orbit and chi-square mass fit to CS ring kinematics
claims.finding: T1 harbors a possible quiescent IMBH

evidence.quote: the observed kinematics of the T1 ring can be explained by a Keplerian orbit around a mass of $M_{\rm dyn}\simeq 1.3 \times 10^4$ $M_\odot$

claims.experiment: Compared kinetic energy with mid-IR luminosity
claims.result: Mid-IR luminosity ~1e2 Lsun vs expected >1e4 Lsun

evidence.quote: Consequently, the protostellar outflow scenario is not plausible for the origin of the broad-velocity-width nature of HCN–0.085–0.094.

claims.hypothesis: The clumps are close to Sgr A*
claims.result: Radio blobs at NE edges of T1–T3
claims.finding: Clumps lie within ~10 pc of Sgr A*

evidence.quote: This indicates that T1, T2 and T3 are located within the central 10 pc of our Galaxy.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Bipolar outflow from massive protostar rejected; dense cluster of dark remnants cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: Although the possibility of a cluster of dark stellar remnants cannot be ruled out yet

limitations_admitted.value: A single source of ~1e4 Msun cannot explain T2 and T3 kinematics; diffuse mass distribution possible

evidence.quote: However, there could be diffuse mass distribution around the point-like mass.
